## Summary

**File:** `JDBCSQLDialect.java` — extracted the duplicated USAGE-bitmask assembly.

The `catalogUsage` and `schemaUsage` blocks in `initDriverSettings` built the same five-flag `SQLDialect.USAGE_*` bitmask (`DML | DDL | PROC | INDEX | PRIV`) from five JDBC `supports…In{DataManipulation,TableDefinitions,ProcedureCalls,IndexDefinitions,PrivilegeDefinitions}` capability calls — identical bit mapping, differing only in catalog-vs-schema method names and the on-error fallback. I pulled the mapping into one well-named helper:

```java
private static int makeUsageFlags(boolean dataManipulation, boolean tableDefinitions,
                                  boolean procedureCalls, boolean indexDefinitions,
                                  boolean privilegeDefinitions) { ... }
```

Each call site now reads as five named capability arguments instead of a ternary-OR soup, and the two distinct error defaults (`USAGE_NONE` for catalog, `USAGE_DDL | USAGE_DML` for schema) are preserved in place.

**Why this is behavior-preserving:** both originals evaluate all five metadata calls eagerly within a single `|` expression (single pipe, no short-circuit) and assign only after the full expression completes; on any exception the whole block falls to its default. My version evaluates the same five calls as arguments inside the same `try`, so an exception in any one still lands in the same `catch` with the same default. Identical semantics.

**What I deliberately did *not* touch in this file:** the rest of `initDriverSettings` is heterogeneous, and the `unquotedIdentCase`/`quotedIdentCase` blocks rely on `if/else-if` **short-circuit** evaluation (`storesLowerCaseIdentifiers()` is only called when the upper check is false). Extracting those into a helper with eager arguments would change which metadata call throws on a failing driver — a real behavior change — so I left them as-is.

**Verification caveat (unchanged):** no compilable build here, so inspection-verified; this change introduces no new types or imports (`SQLDialect` was already imported).

Across the four iterations so far, all changes are confined to the `org.jkiss.dbeaver.model.jdbc` plugin and are behavior-preserving DRY/extraction cleanups. The suspected `Long → Types.SMALLINT` bug in `JDBCUtils.getTypeIdFromValue` remains flagged-but-unchanged pending your call. Want another, or shall I stop here?
